from: A furniture workshop with 50 staff saw labour turnover fall from 34% to 18% a year after a change to its shift roster. It reckons each replacement costs it about N$6 500. Interpret those figures for the owner.
to: A furniture workshop with 50 staff saw labour turnover fall from 34% to 18% a year after a change to its shift roster. It reckons each replacement costs it about N$6 500. Explain what those figures mean for the owner.
why: Interpret is not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Explain. The answer reads the figures against each other and says what they mean, and it asks for more than one paper part, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: A new owner takes over a 30-person engineering workshop and wants to form a view within three months of whether the manager already in post is doing a good job. Set out the questions she should ask about the workshop’s figures and practices before deciding, and say what each one would tell her.
to: A new owner takes over a 30-person engineering workshop and wants to form a view within three months of whether the manager already in post is doing a good job. Identify the questions she should ask about the workshop’s figures and practices before deciding, and explain what each one would tell her.
why: Set out and say are not used on the current AS papers; reworded to Identify and Explain. Several questions are asked for, so no single paper tariff is claimed.

from: Ongwediva Steel has grown from 20 to 95 employees in four years. Analyse what Fayol’s functions and Mintzberg’s roles each reveal about the founder’s working day, and recommend what he should change first.
to: Ongwediva Steel has grown from 20 to 95 employees in four years. Its founder still takes every decision, spends his days dealing with whatever has gone wrong, and has not written a plan since the business started. A consultant tells him he has stopped managing. Analyse what Fayol’s functions and Mintzberg’s roles each reveal about the founder’s working day, and evaluate what he should change first.
